---
title: "Composite targets and criterion directions"
subtitle: "4.6 · after the postrank vignette m2 and theory book, ch. 12 and 19"
description: "Comparison of reporting objectives based on composite values and criterion-specific directions."
---

Directional reporting on separate criteria and reporting on a weighted composite define different targets. Error
weights determine the cost of criterion-specific mistakes; composite coefficients combine target magnitudes.
At the known state A = (1, −2), B = (0, 0), the lower-cost criterion direction can therefore oppose the direction
of an equally weighted composite. Both displays use a common withholding cost and report family. Cross-evaluation
of the selected reports distinguishes the consequences of the two objectives, including changes induced by
rescaling a criterion or transforming the complete finite law.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Different targets.** The criterion-direction costs are .2500, .7500 and .3000 for forward, reverse and
  withholding. The composite costs are 1.0000, .0000 and .3000. One objective picks 1/2; the other picks 2/1.
- **Rescale the second criterion.** The composite value of A becomes .250 and its preferred direction flips.
  The criterion-direction cost .2500 stays the same. The positive multiplier applies to every unit, while error
  weights and composite coefficients keep their separate roles.
- **Composite equality.** Both strict composite directions cost 1.0000. Withholding costs .3000. Each criterion
  still distinguishes the units, but their composite is equal; a shared grade withholds rather than asserting that equality.
- **Two reports, same disclosure.** Every one of the 75 reports is evaluated. Criterion directions choose
  1/2/2/3 with risk .1417; the composite chooses 1/1/2/3 with risk .0333. Both disclose 5 pairs. Both columns evaluate each selected report under the two objectives.
- **Transform the whole law.** Exponentiating every finite input preserves the criterion best report and its
  risk .1417. The composite now selects 1/1/2/2 with risk .0667. The complete criterion best-report sets before
  and after remain visible under the same settings.
- **Rescale the Normal composite.** The first composite mean is .635. This analytic calculation uses the six
  sites’ declared independence across units and criteria; marginal means alone would not specify its uncertainty.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
All examples are synthetic supplied laws. Composite coefficients stay nonnegative and sum to one, matching the
package interface. A positive multiplier changes composite magnitudes; a strictly increasing finite-state
transformation preserves criterion directions without refitting the law. The two risk scales do not choose the
substantive target. No thirty-site joint law is inferred from marginal releases.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
This prints composite scores of posterior means; `weights` are composite coefficients. Package scales divide, so a second-criterion scale of ten
corresponds to the browser’s multiplier .1.

```r
library(postrank)
postrank_composite(pr_tutorial$law$means, weights=c(score_A=.5,score_B=.5), scales=c(score_A=1,score_B=10))
```
:::
